title: Coherent right adjoints are local for proper maps between flat families
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. On the full derived categories of modules with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] has a right adjoint $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ with counit $\varepsilon_f:Rf_*f^!\to\operatorname{id}$. If $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ is any open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], put $U=f^{-1}V$, write $j_X:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_V:U\to V$, and choose the corresponding adjunction for $f_V$. For every locally bounded-below $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$, the canonical mate
$$j_X^*f^!K\longrightarrow f_V^!(j^*K)$$
is an isomorphism. Here locally bounded below means that each point has a neighbourhood on which $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $i$. The mate is the transpose under $Rf_{V,*}\dashv f_V^!$ of the restriction of $\varepsilon_{f,K}$, using the canonical identification $Rf_{V,*}j_X^*\simeq j^*Rf_*$. Thus this isomorphism identifies the restricted counit with $\varepsilon_{f_V,j^*K}$. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $S,X,Y$, no Noetherian hypothesis, and no flatness of $f$ are assumed.

source.place: Tags 0A9E (lemma-twisted-inverse-image), 0A9P (lemma-proper-noetherian), especially its footnote giving proper pseudo-coherent morphisms as the correct generality. Pseudo-coherence here follows from more-morphisms.tex Tags 0695 (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-pseudo-coherent) and 0683 (lemma-permanence-pseudo-coherent). Agent-formulated extension from qcqs schemes by localization on affine target opens and coherent duality descent; the arbitrary-base existence/locality assertion is not claimed to be the literal statement of 0A9E.

proof.text: Use ordinary derived categories throughout. For qcqs $X,Y$, compact generation [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-compact-generation], preservation of coproducts [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-direct-sums] and [lem-pc-brown-representability-right-adjoint] give $Rf_*\dashv a_f$. For arbitrary schemes properness still makes $f$ qcqs. Preservation of quasi-coherence and coproducts therefore gives the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-levelwise-quasicoherent-brown] in its single-scheme case, so $a_f$ exists globally as well. Apply the same argument to every open restriction of $f$. The general ordinary Brown input is needed here because compact generation and the qcqs coherator theorem have qcqs scheme hypotheses; no equivalence $D(\mathrm{QCoh}(X))=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A9E, ordinary Brown proof; general weak-Serre Brown theorem for the arbitrary-scheme existence clause.

proof.text:
First suppose $Y$ is qcqs, $V\subset Y$ is quasi-compact, $U=f^{-1}V$, and $Q\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ restricts to zero on $V$. Then $X$ is qcqs and $U$ is quasi-compact. For any perfect $P$ on $X$ and any $b:P\to f^!Q$, take its adjoint $c:Rf_*P\to Q$. The object $Rf_*P$ is pseudo-coherent by [lem-sfb-flat-family-perfect-direct-image-pseudocoherent]. The supported-map annihilation theorem supplies $I\to\mathcal O_Y$, perfect and invertible on $V$, such that $I\otimes^L Rf_*P\to Q$ is zero. The projection formula identifies its source with $Rf_*(Lf^*I\otimes^L P)$. Naturality of adjunction identifies the transpose with
$$Lf^*I\otimes^L P\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{b}f^!Q.$$
It is therefore zero. On $U$ its first arrow is an isomorphism, so $b|_U=0$. The perfect open-support detector now gives $(f^!Q)|_U=0$. This uses boundedness only for $Q$, in the pseudo-coherent case of the annihilation theorem; it assumes no flatness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0A9P, lemma-proper-noetherian, proof and footnote; Tag 0A9C, lemma-map-from-pseudo-coherent-to-complex-with-support.

proof.text: For qcqs $Y$ and quasi-compact $V$, the preceding support argument and [lem-sc-right-adjoint-open-support-criterion] give the isomorphism $j_X^*a_fK\to a_{f_V}j^*K$ for $K\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$. It is the transpose of $Rf_{V,*}j_X^*a_fK\simeq j^*Rf_*a_fK\xrightarrow{j^*\varepsilon_f}j^*K$, using [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. For successive opens, transposing the composite of the two mates gives the restriction of $\varepsilon_f$: first use $\varepsilon_{f_V}Rf_{V,*}(\text{first mate})=j^*\varepsilon_f$, then the analogous equation for the second mate. This is also the transpose of the direct mate, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves equality. Identity restriction gives the identity by the same equation. This is an ordinary counit calculation.

source.place: Tags 0A9L, 0A9N and 0A9P; ordinary transpose and successive-restriction counit equations.

proof.text: For a set-indexed open cover $Y=\bigcup_iY_i$, form its face-only Cech schemes $Y_n$ and $X_n=X\times_Y Y_n$, with augmentations $b,a$. Work in the ordinary total module categories of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category], and let $\mathcal L_X,\mathcal L_Y$ mean levelwise quasi-coherent derived objects, without a cartesian condition. The free evaluation adjoints $\ell_n\dashv e_n$ are exact by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint]. Thus evaluation preserves K-injectives: for an acyclic complex $A$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(A,e_nI)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(\ell_nA,I)=0$. The underived total pushforward along $(f_n)$ is defined componentwise using open restriction/pushforward comparison for its transitions. Resolve in the total module category by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Its right derived functor $F$ consequently satisfies $e_nF=Rf_{n,*}e_n$. It preserves levelwise quasi-coherence and coproducts by the respective qcqs-morphism theorems and conservative evaluations. These are constructions on complexes in ordinary abelian categories.

source.place: Ordinary total-site construction, spaces-simplicial.tex Tags 0D72 and 0D9E; K-injective computation and open restriction.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-levelwise-quasicoherent-brown] to $F:\mathcal L_X\to\mathcal L_Y$ to obtain $F\dashv G$. On each $\alpha$-labelled summand of $e_m\ell_n$, open restriction and [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] show that the canonical comparison $\ell_n^YRf_{n,*}M\to F\ell_n^XM$, the transpose under $\ell_n^Y\dashv e_n$ of $Rf_{n,*}$ applied to the unit $M\to e_n\ell_n^XM$ (using $e_nF=Rf_{n,*}e_n$), is an isomorphism on every component; the finite direct sums in the free formula commute with $Rf_{m,*}$, and conservativity of the evaluations makes it an isomorphism $F\ell_n^X\simeq\ell_n^Y Rf_{n,*}$. Whenever $a_n$ is the right adjoint of $Rf_{n,*}$, for $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X_n)$ and $N\in\mathcal L_Y$ the adjunctions give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,e_nGN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\ell_n^XM,GN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F\ell_n^XM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{n,*}M,e_nN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,a_ne_nN).$$
Hence Yoneda identifies $e_nG\simeq a_ne_n$. Its normalization is $e_n\varepsilon_F=\varepsilon_{f_n}$ under these identifications, since all four bijections send identities to the specified counits.

source.place: Total-category Brown and the exact free-evaluation adjunction; component Hom calculation.

proof.text:
The transition of this actual total object is determined by the free-evaluation counit. Indeed the $\alpha$ summand of $\ell_me_mGN\to GN$ is precisely $\theta^{GN}_\alpha$ by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint]. The normalization in the previous step and naturality of $\varepsilon_F$ show that its transpose is $\theta^N_\alpha\circ\operatorname{res}_\alpha(\varepsilon_{f_m})$. Thus, under $e_nGN=a_ne_nN$,
$$\theta^{GN}_\alpha=(a_n\theta^N_\alpha)\circ\mu_{\alpha,e_mN},$$
where $\mu_\alpha:\operatorname{res}_\alpha a_m\to a_n\operatorname{res}_\alpha$ is the ordinary open-square mate. This also proves the equation for the counit, not merely an isomorphism of component objects. The identity and composition equations hold because $GN$ is already an object of the total derived category; no lifting of a diagram in derived categories is being asserted.

source.place: Tag 0D72 free-adjunction inverse formula and Tag 0D9E derived free counit; naturality of the ordinary total counit.

proof.text: First suppose $Y$ is quasi-separated, and choose an affine open cover. Each nonempty finite intersection $Y_{i_0\ldots i_n}$ is qcqs: it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] (iterate using finite affine covers of the earlier intersections) and is an open subscheme of an affine scheme. Its inverse image under the proper $f$ is qcqs. Thus each $a_n$ in the preceding construction is defined componentwise on the disjoint union, using the qcqs Brown adjoints of step 1. Module complexes, K-injective resolutions and their Hom bijections on a disjoint union are componentwise, so these component adjoints form an adjoint on the whole disjoint union. For locally bounded-below $K$, its restriction to each intersection has a single lower bound, obtained from a finite subcover and the minimum of the finitely many local bounds. Step 3 makes every transition mate at these inputs invertible. For $N=b^*K$, the equation of step 6 therefore makes $GN$ cartesian.

source.place: Qcqs localization of Tag 0A9P; finite intersections for a quasi-separated target and componentwise resolutions.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-zariski-total-quasicoherent-descent] to this cartesian total object to obtain $H\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ with $a^*H\simeq Gb^*K$. For every $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$, the object $Fa^*M$ has components $Rf_{n,*}(M|_{X_n})$ and transitions the restriction isomorphisms of [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open], so it is cartesian. The total pushforward of step 4 is the direct image of the ringed total morphism given levelwise by $f_n$, and $b\circ(f_n)=f\circ a$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives $Rb_*Fa^*M\simeq Rf_*Ra_*a^*M\simeq Rf_*M$, the last by the unit isomorphism of the descent equivalence on $X$. The descent equivalence on $Y$ therefore identifies $Fa^*M\simeq b^*Rb_*Fa^*M\simeq b^*Rf_*M$, naturally in $M$. Consequently
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L_X}(a^*M,Gb^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L_Y}(Fa^*M,b^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*M,K).$$
Thus $H\simeq a_fK$ by the representing bijections, and the image of its identity gives the global counit. Its component on every affine chart is the local counit by step 5. In particular the canonical mate to each chart is invertible. Full faithfulness here concerns actual total derived objects via the descent equivalence, not compatible families of ordinary derived morphisms.

source.place: Ordinary total descent, sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D7V; representability and counit normalization.

proof.text: For quasi-separated $Y$, the preceding proof allows any affine cover, so include any specified affine open $W$ as a chart; it proves locality to $W$. Let $V\subset Y$ be any open. It too is quasi-separated, and $K|_V$ is locally bounded below. For each affine $W\subset V$, apply the chart result to $Y\supset W$ and $V\supset W$. The successive-restriction counit calculation of step 3 factors the mate from $Y$ to $W$ as the restriction of the mate from $Y$ to $V$ followed by the mate from $V$ to $W$. Both the direct mate and the second factor are isomorphisms. Thus the first factor is an isomorphism over $f^{-1}W$. These opens cover $f^{-1}V$, so every cohomology sheaf of the cone of the mate vanishes, proving locality for arbitrary $V$.

source.place: Extension from affine-chart locality to arbitrary opens by counit pasting and stalkwise cone detection.

proof.text: Now allow arbitrary $Y$ and choose an affine cover again. A finite intersection of these charts may fail to be quasi-compact, but it is an open subscheme of an affine scheme, so its open immersion into that affine is separated (its relative diagonal is an isomorphism). Hence [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] makes it separated and thus quasi-separated: a closed-immersion diagonal is quasi-compact by the cited definitions. The already proved quasi-separated case applies to the restricted proper map on each intersection and every further face open, with locally bounded-below $K$. Run the same total construction of steps 4--6: the level adjoints exist by step 1 and their transition mates at $b^*K$ are now isomorphisms by step 9. Thus $Gb^*K$ is cartesian. Step 8's ordinary descent and Hom calculation again identify its descent with $a_fK$, including its counit and locality to every affine chart. This second pass does not impose quasi-compactness on the intersections or a uniform lower bound across them. The family hypotheses persist on all source and target opens.

source.place: Second ordinary Cech pass: separated intersections of affine opens on an arbitrary scheme; same total adjunction and descent calculation.

proof.text: The argument of step 9 now applies without quasi-separatedness: for any $V\subset Y$, cover $V$ by affine opens $W$, use the just proved arbitrary-target chart result for $Y\supset W$ and $V\supset W$, and use ordinary counit pasting. It follows that the specified mate $j_X^*a_fK\to a_{f_V}j^*K$ is invertible. Its defining transpose is the restricted counit, so it identifies that counit with $\varepsilon_{f_V}$ exactly as claimed.

source.place: Arbitrary-open conclusion from affine-chart locality and the counit formula.

proof.text: Identity and successive restriction compatibility are the transpose equations proved in step 3, which did not use qcqs hypotheses. For an isomorphism of $S$-diagrams, transport the functors and adjunction bijections. The ordinary comparisons of [lem-sfb-coherent-right-adjoint-comparisons] identify the transported adjoints with the chosen ones by the unique counit-preserving isomorphisms and satisfy their cocycle equations. Both transported and original restriction mates transpose to the same restricted counit after the canonical direct-image comparisons, hence agree by injectivity of the adjunction bijection. This proves naturality in $K$ and all stated coherence independently of all chosen Brown representatives and covers.

source.place: Ordinary uniqueness of right adjoints and naturality of the counit transpose; no enhanced mates.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. On the full derived categories of modules with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] has a right adjoint $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ with counit $\varepsilon_f:Rf_*f^!\to\operatorname{id}$. If $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ is any open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], put $U=f^{-1}V$, write $j_X:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_V:U\to V$, and choose the corresponding adjunction for $f_V$. For every locally bounded-below $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$, the canonical mate
$$j_X^*f^!K\longrightarrow f_V^!(j^*K)$$
is an isomorphism. Here locally bounded below means that each point has a neighbourhood on which $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $i$. The mate is the transpose under $Rf_{V,*}\dashv f_V^!$ of the restriction of $\varepsilon_{f,K}$, using the canonical identification $Rf_{V,*}j_X^*\simeq j^*Rf_*$. Thus this isomorphism identifies the restricted counit with $\varepsilon_{f_V,j^*K}$. These canonical identifications respect identity opens, successive restrictions and isomorphisms of the $S$-diagram. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $S,X,Y$, no Noetherian hypothesis, and no flatness of $f$ are assumed.
